title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs Placed in Solitary After Prison Fight at Fort Dix
excerpt: The music mogul was moved to administrative segregation after a physical altercation with a fellow inmate at the New Jersey federal facility where he is serving a 50-month sentence.
body:
• Sean 'Diddy' Combs was placed in solitary confinement at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey after a physical altercation with another inmate earlier this week.
  • The fight reportedly started after the other inmate made disparaging remarks toward Combs, with staff intervening quickly to separate the men.
  • Combs, 56, is serving a 50-month sentence on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution, with a release date currently set for February 2028.
  • The incident could affect his release timeline, which had recently been moved up due to good conduct credits and program participation.

Sean "Diddy" Combs has been placed in solitary confinement after getting into a physical altercation with a fellow inmate at the Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix in New Jersey, according to reports from NBC News, TMZ and ABC News.

The fight occurred earlier this week at the low-security federal facility, which sits on a military base outside Philadelphia and houses over 4,000 inmates. Multiple sources told TMZ that the confrontation began after another inmate made disparaging remarks toward Combs, escalating into pushing and punching before correctional officers intervened.

Combs, 56, reportedly "held his own" during the exchange, according to one source cited by TMZ. The Federal Bureau of Prisons declined to comment on the incident, citing privacy and security concerns.

Release Date at Risk

The altercation raises questions about Combs's release timeline. His expected release date had recently been moved up to February 8, 2028, from an earlier projection of April 2028, credited to good conduct time and participation in approved programs including a drug abuse treatment program.

https://x.com/Bubblebathgirl/status/2080656312757530669

The timeline has shifted multiple times during his incarceration. In November 2025, his release date was pushed back by several months to June 2028, days after his representative denied reports that Combs had created and consumed alcohol behind bars. It was subsequently moved forward again.

It remains unclear whether the reported fight will trigger a formal disciplinary review or affect his projected release. Neither FCI Fort Dix nor the Bureau of Prisons has confirmed whether Combs remains in solitary confinement.

Background: Trial and Conviction

The Bad Boy Records founder was sentenced to 50 months in federal prison in October 2025 by U.S. District Judge Arun Subramanian. A jury found him guilty on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution, related to the transportation of two former girlfriends — Casandra "Cassie" Ventura Fine and an anonymous accuser identified as "Jane" — as well as sex workers.

Combs was acquitted of the more serious charges of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion. His attorneys had argued for no more than 14 months imprisonment, while prosecutors sought at least 11 years. He has denied all allegations of sexual misconduct.

"We are not at liberty to disclose or provide internal information pertaining to any inmate in our custody. Such information would not be available for the public domain."

— FCI Fort Dix spokesperson, to TMZ

Legal Battles Continue

Combs's legal team is pursuing an appeal of his conviction. Beyond the criminal case, he faces upwards of 70 civil lawsuits across the country stemming from allegations of drugging, sexual assault and coercion. The most recent, filed on June 9, comes from a former child actor who alleges Combs sexually assaulted him during a networking event in 2007. Combs's representative has called those allegations "false and ridiculous."

Prior to sentencing, Combs wrote to the judge that he had gotten sober "for the first time in 25 years" and had been attending therapy and mentoring fellow inmates. He was transferred from Brooklyn's Metropolitan Detention Center to Fort Dix, which his legal team had requested due to the facility's drug rehabilitation program and proximity to his family.
